slides.purpose: State the answer and the ask up front
slides.headline: Growth slowed because churn rose, not because sales slowed: restore onboarding now (€0.8M) and gate the €3.6M AE hire on retention
slides.reason_to_exist: Board reads the answer and the asks on one page

slides.purpose: Locate the slowdown in the ARR bridge
slides.headline: Net new ARR fell by €5.6M: churn rose by €4.5M and expansion fell by €1.3M while new ARR grew by €0.2M
slides.reason_to_exist: The single exhibit that relocates the problem from sales to retention

slides.decision_role: rejects the premise of the current plan
slides.headline: The sales engine held: pipeline rose from €38.9M to €45.9M, win rate stayed between 23% and 24%, and only 17% of churned customers left for a competitor
slides.reason_to_exist: The current plan rests on this diagnosis; the board needs to see it tested
slides.why_not_merge: S2 shows where ARR was lost; S3 disproves the alternative explanation the plan relies on. Merging would bury the test of the current plan.

slides.purpose: Show churn concentration in first-year customers
slides.headline: First-year customers churned 26% of ARR versus 9% for mature ones and produced 60.3% of churned ARR
slides.reason_to_exist: Shows the problem is onboarding of new customers, not the installed base

slides.purpose: Link the churn to the onboarding cut and price the saving
slides.headline: Cutting onboarding from 14 to 6 saved €0.8M but time to first value rose from 21 to 48 days and excess first-year churn cost about €2.5M
slides.reason_to_exist: Turns the diagnosis into a costed, reversible decision
slides.why_not_merge: S4 shows where churn sits; S5 shows why and what it cost. One slide would carry two exhibits and two messages.

slides.headline: The CRO's €9M is a full-productivity run-rate: assuming a linear 9-month ramp, 30 AEs add about €5.6M in 2026, €3.4M short, for €3.6M a year
slides.reason_to_exist: The board is asked to approve this number

slides.purpose: Compare options on the same cost and risk components
slides.headline: Restoring onboarding first costs €0.8M against €3.6M for the CRO plan and €4.4M for doing both, and removes the €2.5M churn exposure
slides.reason_to_exist: Same-basis comparison of the three options the board can choose

slides.purpose: Size the levers against the target and admit the gap
slides.headline: Retention levers recover up to €3.8M of the €5.6M lost; gated AE hiring closes the remaining €1.8M, mostly in 2027
slides.reason_to_exist: Reconciles levers to the target and states the gap honestly
slides.why_not_merge: S7 chooses the option; S8 shows what it delivers and what it leaves open.

slides.headline: Board asks today: approve €0.8M for onboarding, reject the Q1 30-AE hire, pre-approve the €3.6M AE envelope behind a Q2 retention gate
slides.reason_to_exist: Turns the recommendation into decisions, a gate and tracking KPIs
slides.why_not_merge: The executive summary states the answer; this slide lists the decisions, gate and KPIs the board approves. Merging would overload the opening page.
